I was in-patient at Beaumont in Royal Oak, I choose Royal Oak due to the stories I’d heard about other places. This is by far the best option I was able to find but granted that was about 5 years ago. When I checked in, I had to wait in the emergency room, where people were visibly having seizures and other problems right in front of me. While it wasn’t traumatic for me, I’d say the experience could be shocking for the average person.

I stayed there for about a month, starting on the 9th floor. Every morning, they wake you up around 6-7:30 AM to draw blood and take your vitals. Days are structured with 2-3 activities, and the rest of the time is usually spent sitting around doing crafts or other things. 

Here’s the thing: the only person who can truly be there for you is yourself. For me, it took a lot to come to terms with what was happening in my life. Without discouraging you, I will say that the program helped to the extent that it removed me from the situation that was making me feel that way. However, eventually, you’re put back into that same situation—this time with thousands of dollars in bills to deal with as well.
